bravas.title: Air fryer patatas bravas with homemade paprika sauce
bravas.summary: Golden air fryer potatoes with a smooth, tomato-free paprika sauce. A Spanish sharing tapa with batch-cooking guidance and adjustable heat.
bravas.notes: Cut 2 cm cubes. Use an air fryer of at least 5 litres; allow about 25 extra minutes for a second batch if crowded. Contains wheat. Keep potatoes and sauce separately at 4 °C or below for up to 2 days and reheat thoroughly. Add sauce just before serving.
ingredients: olive oil: 15 g for potatoes, 20 g for sauce
steps: Cut the potatoes
Cut 800 g peeled potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Rinse and dry thoroughly with a clean towel so the surfaces can brown.
Prepare the air fryer
Preheat to 190 °C for 3 minutes if required by your appliance. Toss potatoes with 15 g oil and 2 g salt.
Cook without crowding
Spread potatoes with space around them. Cook at 190 °C for 20 minutes, shaking halfway through. Use two batches if necessary.
Soften onion and garlic
Meanwhile, chop onion and garlic. Soften the onion in 20 g oil for 8 minutes, then add garlic for 1 minute.
Cook flour and paprika
Stir in 10 g flour for 1 minute. Remove from the heat, add both paprikas and stir briefly without scorching.
Finish the sauce
Gradually whisk in 250 ml stock. Simmer 5 minutes, add vinegar and 1 g salt, then blend until smooth.
Check the potatoes
Increase to 200 °C and cook for another 3–5 minutes. Check for tender centres and golden edges; extend cooking if needed.
Serve with sauce
Divide into four tapa portions. Spoon hot sauce over just before eating and serve any remaining sauce separately.
faq: Does bravas sauce need tomatoes?
Not this version: flour and stock thicken it, while paprika gives colour. Other versions include tomatoes.
Why are my potatoes soft?
Excess moisture or a crowded basket prevents browning. Dry thoroughly and cook in batches.
How do I reduce the heat?
Replace the 1 g hot paprika with another 1 g sweet paprika.

pizza.title: Pizza beans with tomato and mozzarella
pizza.summary: White beans baked in tomato sauce with golden mozzarella: a simple pantry dinner in one skillet, ready in 45 minutes without making pizza dough.
pizza.notes: Use fully cooked, drained canned beans, never raw dried beans. Use a 26 cm ovenproof skillet or transfer to a baking dish before baking. Contains milk. Bread is not included in the ingredients or nutrition. Refrigerate within 2 hours, keep at 4 °C or below up to 3 days and reheat thoroughly.
ingredients: canned white beans, cooked and drained
steps: Drain and prepare
Rinse and drain 700 g cooked beans. Chop onion and garlic. Preheat a conventional oven to 220 °C / 425 °F.
Soften the onion
Heat 20 g oil in a 26 cm ovenproof skillet. Cook the onion over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring.
Add garlic and paste
Stir in garlic and 20 g tomato paste. Cook 1 minute until aromatic, without burning.
Reduce the tomatoes
Add 500 g crushed tomatoes, 1 g oregano and 2 g salt. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the beans
Gently fold in drained beans without breaking them. Heat for 3 minutes; the sauce should coat them without becoming dry.
Top with mozzarella
Turn off the heat. Scatter 150 g mozzarella and the remaining 1 g oregano over the surface without stirring.
Bake until golden
Bake at 220 °C / 425 °F for 5–8 minutes until the cheese melts and browns. Use oven gloves: the handle is hot too.
Rest and serve
Rest on a heatproof trivet for 5 minutes, then serve four hot portions with intact beans and golden cheese.
faq: Can I start with dried beans?
Cook them completely according to the packet first, then weigh 700 g drained. That extra time is not included.
Can I use chickpeas?
Yes, fully cooked and drained, although texture and nutrition change.
Can I skip the oven?
Cover over low heat to melt the cheese; it will not develop a browned top.

spekulatius.title: Apple and Spekulatius dessert cups
spekulatius.summary: Six no-bake dessert cups with cooked apple, spiced Spekulatius biscuits and a light-textured yogurt cream. No eggs, with chilling time included.
spekulatius.notes: Use spiced Spekulatius biscuits, not biscuit spread. Contains milk and wheat; check biscuits for nuts. Cool apples fully before layering. Resting time includes 20 minutes to cool apples and 2 hours chilling. Keep covered at 4 °C or below up to 2 days; add the final crumbs when serving.
ingredients: sugar: 20 g for apples, 20 g for cream
steps: Dice the apples
Dice 500 g prepared apples. Place in a saucepan with 40 ml water, lemon juice, cinnamon and 20 g sugar.
Cook the compote
Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring. Leave some tender pieces; uncover briefly if too wet.
Cool completely
Spread in a shallow container and cool for about 20 minutes. Refrigerate while preparing cream; never layer it while hot.
Crush the biscuits
Coarsely crush 150 g biscuits in a food bag. Reserve 30 g dry crumbs for serving.
Whip the cream
Whip 200 g cold cream with the remaining 20 g sugar to soft peaks. Stop before it becomes grainy.
Fold in yogurt
Stir 300 g yogurt until smooth. Gently fold in whipped cream in two additions, keeping the mixture airy.
Layer and chill
Divide 120 g crumbs, cold apples and cream among six 200 ml glasses. Cover and refrigerate for 2 hours.
Finish the cups
Add the reserved 30 g crumbs just before serving. Serve cold, one glass per person.
faq: Can I make these a day ahead?
Yes. Refrigerate covered and keep the final crumbs dry until serving.
What replaces Spekulatius?
Spiced cinnamon or ginger biscuits work, with a different flavour and nutrition.
Why is the cream runny?
Warm apples, thin yogurt or underwhipped cream can loosen it. Use cold ingredients and chill fully.

tartiflette.title: Reblochon tartiflette with potatoes and bacon
tartiflette.summary: A bubbling French potato bake with onion, smoked bacon and Reblochon. Six portions, with clear guidance for arranging the cheese rind-side up.
tartiflette.notes: Use waxy potatoes and Reblochon; Camembert makes an adaptation with a different flavour. Contains milk. Bacon and cheese are salty: taste before adding salt. Three minutes of simmering does not remove all wine alcohol; water can replace it. Use a 25 × 20 cm dish. Refrigerate within 2 hours and keep up to 3 days at 4 °C or below; reheat thoroughly.
steps: Slice and boil potatoes
Cut potatoes into 8 mm slices. Start in cold water, bring to a boil and simmer 10–12 minutes until almost tender.
Drain carefully
Drain and let steam-dry for 5 minutes. Preheat a conventional oven to 200 °C / 400 °F.
Brown the bacon
Cook bacon in a wide dry skillet over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring, until fat renders and edges brown.
Add onion and wine
Add sliced onion and cook 8 minutes. Pour in 100 ml wine and simmer 3 minutes to reduce the liquid.
Prepare the cheese
Split Reblochon horizontally, keeping its rind. Cut one half into chunks and the other into two pieces for the top.
Assemble the dish
Rub the dish with halved garlic. Combine potatoes, bacon, onion, pepper and cheese chunks. Lay remaining cheese on top, rind-side up.
Bake until bubbling
Bake at 200 °C / 400 °F for 20–25 minutes until potatoes are tender and cheese is melted and golden. Cover loosely if browning too fast.
Rest and serve
Rest outside the oven for 5 minutes. Serve six hot portions, scooping potatoes, bacon and cheese from the full depth.
faq: Should I remove the rind?
Keep the edible rind and place the top pieces rind-side up.
Can I omit wine?
Replace with 100 ml water. Brief cooking of wine does not guarantee an alcohol-free dish.
Can I use another cheese?
Camembert is an accessible adaptation, but the reference dish uses Reblochon.

zucca.title: Pumpkin and ricotta pasta bake without béchamel
zucca.summary: Rigatoni baked in roasted pumpkin and ricotta sauce, with a golden mozzarella topping. Four portions, without béchamel, with tips to keep the pasta creamy.
zucca.notes: Weigh 600 g pumpkin after peeling and removing seeds. Use a 24 × 20 cm dish. Contains wheat and milk. Undercook pasta before baking and adjust sauce with its cooking water. Refrigerate within 2 hours, keep up to 3 days at 4 °C or below and add a splash of water before reheating thoroughly.
ingredients: dried short pasta, such as rigatoni
steps: Prepare the pumpkin
Preheat to 200 °C / 400 °F. Cut pumpkin into 2 cm cubes; toss with oil, chopped garlic, 2 g salt and pepper.
Roast until tender
Spread on a tray and roast 25–30 minutes, turning once, until soft with lightly browned edges.
Cook the pasta
Boil pasta in water with the remaining 3 g salt. Drain 2 minutes before the packet time, reserving 150 ml cooking water.
Blend the sauce
Blend roasted pumpkin, ricotta and 100 ml cooking water until smooth. Add the remaining water if needed for a flowing sauce.
Combine with pasta
Mix pasta and sauce in a large bowl. Fold in 60 g mozzarella and 15 g Parmesan, coating all the tubes.
Top the dish
Transfer to a 24 × 20 cm dish. Top with the remaining 60 g mozzarella and 15 g Parmesan.
Bake the pasta
Bake at 200 °C / 400 °F for 15–20 minutes until edges bubble and cheese browns, keeping the pasta underneath creamy.
Rest and portion
Rest 5 minutes outside the oven, then serve four portions with some golden topping and creamy sauce from the bottom.
faq: Can I assemble it ahead?
Cover and refrigerate until the next day. Bake longer from chilled and check the centre is thoroughly hot.
Why is it dry?
The sauce may be too thick or pasta overcooked. Keep the sauce slightly loose when assembling.
Is there béchamel?
No. Pumpkin and ricotta make the sauce; cooking water adjusts its consistency.

seiro.title: Seiro steamed pork and cabbage with sesame sauce
seiro.summary: Thin pork slices steamed with cabbage and carrots, served with sesame and soy dipping sauce. Includes basket arrangement and doneness checks.
seiro.notes: Use pork loin sliced 2 mm thick, not ground pork or thick steaks. Fit a 24 cm bamboo steamer securely to its pot, following manufacturer guidance, or use a covered metal steamer. Contains sesame, soy and usually wheat. Leave steam holes clear and never let the pot boil dry. Refrigerate within 2 hours, keep at 4 °C or below up to 2 days and reheat thoroughly.
steps: Set up the steamer
Dampen bamboo according to its instructions. Bring water to a boil below the basket without touching it, checking that the steamer sits securely.
Cut the vegetables
Cut cabbage into 4 cm pieces and carrot into 2 mm slices. Reserve larger leaves to partly line the base.
Separate the pork
Separate pork slices so they do not clump. Halve long pieces and keep chilled until assembling.
Arrange loose layers
Partly line the basket with cabbage, leaving gaps. Add carrots and remaining cabbage, interleaving unfolded pork slices without packing tightly.
Steam the food
Set over boiling water, cover and steam 15–18 minutes. Maintain steady steam and top up the pot with hot water if necessary.
Mix sesame sauce
Whisk tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, 20 ml water, sugar and grated ginger until pourable. Use utensils that have not touched raw meat.
Check and rest
Use a thermometer to check the pork centre reaches 75 °C / 167 °F and stays there at least 1 minute; cook longer if needed. Remove and rest covered 3 minutes.
Serve sauce separately
Lift the lid away from your face to release steam safely. Serve two portions of pork and vegetables with sesame sauce alongside.
faq: Can I use a metal steamer?
Yes, with a lid, stable base and water below the food. Check pork doneness with a thermometer.
Can I substitute chicken?
Yes, in thin slices. Keep the same target of 75 °C / 167 °F at the centre for at least 1 minute, checking with a thermometer; timing may change.
Why does it cook unevenly?
Packed meat or blocked holes restrict steam. Spread slices loosely and use batches if needed.

morango.title: Morango cravejado: crunchy strawberry bonbons
morango.summary: Brazilian strawberries wrapped in white brigadeiro and a white confectionery shell studded with red caramel pieces. Makes ten bonbons, with cooling time included.
morango.notes: Use ten firm, fully dry strawberries, about 25 g each. Use white confectionery coating that needs no tempering; real white chocolate requires a different process. Contains milk and may contain soy. Sugar syrup at 150 °C causes burns: use a thermometer, dry equipment and cool completely before handling. Keep at 4 °C or below and eat within 24 hours. Commercial shelf life has not been validated.
ingredients: firm strawberries, cleaned and fully dried, about ten
water-soluble red food colouring, manufacturer dose
white confectionery coating requiring no tempering
steps: Clean and dry fruit
Wash and completely dry strawberries on clean paper. Remove leaves without puncturing flesh. Refrigerate and line a tray with baking parchment.
Cook the brigadeiro
Combine condensed milk, cream, milk powder and butter. Stir over medium-low heat 10–15 minutes until the mixture pulls away from the pan bottom when tilted.
Chill the mixture
Spread in a shallow container, cover the surface and cool 20 minutes. Refrigerate 2 hours or until cold and firm enough to shape.
Make red caramel
Combine sugar, water, vinegar and colouring in a dry saucepan before heating. Boil without stirring until a candy thermometer reads 150 °C / 302 °F.
Cool and crush
Carefully pour a thin layer onto a heatproof silicone mat. Cool completely, about 20 minutes, then crush into small pieces inside a food bag.
Wrap the strawberries
Divide cold brigadeiro into ten portions. Flatten with clean, lightly dampened hands, enclose each dry strawberry without gaps and refrigerate.
Dip the bonbons
Melt coating according to its packet. When fluid and lukewarm, fold in cold caramel pieces. Dip each wrapped strawberry using a fork, drain and place on parchment.
Set and serve
Let the shell set as directed, then refrigerate. Serve ten bonbons; halve one to show its layers. Eat within 24 hours.
faq: Is this morango do amor?
It shares the fruit and brigadeiro, but has caramel chips in a white shell rather than a continuous red shell.
Why does the coating become damp?
Fruit releases water and caramel absorbs moisture. Dry fruit thoroughly, do not puncture it and eat within 24 hours.
Can I sell these?
Calculate ingredients, packaging, energy, labour and waste per unit. Validate local hygiene, storage and shelf-life requirements before selling.
